title: Hierarchical cost bands and GPU provisioning with graceful fallback model variants
creator: Aisha Reynolds
description: Goal: implement a hierarchical cost-band routing system that classifies incoming requests into discrete cost bands (e.g., premium/standard/eco) and matches them to a GPU provisioning profile with spot/on-demand heuristics and precomputed fallback model variants. This ticket covers: (1) cost-band evaluation and tagging at the request ingress, (2) GPU selection policy that prefers cheaper SKUs and spot pools while respecting soft budget caps per-customer and per-region, (3) eviction-risk scoring to add headroom and avoid mid-request spot evictions, and (4) deterministic fallback routing to smaller/quantized model variants when budget or capacity constraints are hit.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Requests are tagged with a cost_band header (premium | standard | eco) based on token budget + customer tier; 2) Routing layer selects GPU pool and spot preference according to band policy; 3) If estimated spend exceeds soft budget cap the request is routed to fallback model variant or queued per policy; 4) Telemetry exposes per-band metrics (cost_per_token, avg_latency_ms, fallback_rate, spot_eviction_rate); 5) Rollout feature flag allows canary to 10% of customer traffic and automatic rollback if fallback_rate > 2% or 95th latency regresses > 30% relative to baseline.
notes:
Design trade-offs considered:
- Hard caps vs soft caps: hard caps cause failures for critical customers; chosen: soft caps with throttling + graceful fallback.
- Spot-first preference reduces cost but increases eviction risk; mitigation: per-region headroom and pre-eviction migration to on-demand for in-flight sessions nearing budget boundary.
- GPU granularity: per-host vs per-pool classification. Chosen: pool-level classification with skip lists for incompatible models.
- Fallback variant selection: prefer quantized or distilled variants with functionally equivalent APIs to preserve structured output compatibility.
implementation_plan:
Milestones:
- Week 1: implement cost-band evaluator + request tagging at ingress (middleware).
- Week 2: proto routing policy module with simple pool selection and spot preference toggles.
- Week 3: integrate eviction-risk scoring and soft-budget check; add deterministic fallback manager.
- Week 4: add telemetry, dashboards, unit + e2e tests; run canary.
Deliverables: routing-policy library, config schema, rollout runbook, Grafana dashboard panels.
rollout_plan:
Phase A: internal canary (10% of infra traffic) behind feature flag; monitor fallback_rate, cost delta, latency.
Phase B: pilot with 5 external customers (non-enterprise) opting into cost-savings mode.
Phase C: full ramp with gradual expansion of spot preference and tighter budget caps per customer types.
Fallback: immediate rollback on high-severity regressions; automatic per-customer rollback if soft cap triggers repeatedly.
metrics: Primary: cost_per_token_usd (per-band), avg_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, fallback_rate_pct, spot_eviction_rate_pct, requests_routed_to_on_demand_pct. Secondary: GPU_utilization_by_pool, queued_request_count, billing_delta_monthly.
benchmarks:
Initial microbench results (internal):
- ECO band w/ spot-first: cost/token -30% vs baseline, p95 latency +18ms.
- Standard band w/ spot-hedging: cost/token -12%, p95 latency +6ms.
Links: https://perf.redwood.ai/bench/ENG-90234-summary
comments: 2026-02-20 Aisha Reynolds: Created ticket after architecture review. Initial design doc uploaded to Confluence.
2026-02-25 Marco Diaz: Implemented ingress tagger prototype; pushed branch with unit tests. See PR #784. Needs review from infra team for performance.
2026-03-01 SRE Review (Liu Chen): Concerned about increased control-plane load when embedding eviction-risk scoring; suggested moving scoring to edge caches and sampling at 10% initially.
2026-03-04 Product feedback (Samir Patel): Add explicit per-customer enforceable hard cap opt-in for enterprise customers; noted in notes and added config flag 'hard_cap_enforce'.
2026-03-07 Design review (Ruth Kim): Fallback UX for API clients should include structured 'fallback_reason' and 'effective_model' fields so SDKs can surface to callers.
2026-03-09 Marco Diaz: Canary rollout started internally at 5% traffic. Observed fallback_rate=0.8% for eco band, spot_eviction_rate=0.4%. Costs trending -18% for eco band.
2026-03-10 Aisha Reynolds: Updated acceptance criteria to add rollback thresholds; added Grafana panels and alert playbook.
final_decision: Adopt hierarchical cost-bands with soft budget caps + deterministic fallback to quantized/distilled variants; spot preference enabled per-band with per-region headroom and sampling-based eviction scoring. Enterprise hard-cap opt-in will be implemented as an escape hatch.
